outline.chapter_title: Introduction: The Efficiency Crisis in Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter sets the stage by discussing the rapid growth of LLMs, the associated challenges regarding energy consumption, memory bandwidth, and deployment costs. It introduces the concept of quantization as a solution and transitions from post-training methods to training-aware low-bit architectures, culminating in the introduction of the 'Era of 1-bit LLMs' and the specific contribution of BitNet b1.58.
subtopics: The Scaling Dilemma: Performance vs. Environmental/Economic Cost
Limitations of Post-Training Quantization (PTQ)
The Promise of Training-Aware Low-Bit Architectures
From Binary to Ternary: Defining the 1.58-Bit Paradigm
Overview of BitNet b1.58 Contributions

outline.description: Before diving into the specific architecture, this chapter reviews the necessary background knowledge for students. It covers standard floating-point representations, the mechanics of matrix multiplication in Transformers, and the theoretical underpinnings of quantization, specifically focusing on why moving from FP16 to integer or ternary domains reduces computational complexity.
subtopics: Floating Point (FP16/BF16) vs. Integer Arithmetic
Matrix Multiplication Costs: Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) Operations
Memory Bandwidth Bottlenecks: DRAM vs. SRAM
Quantization Basics: Uniform vs. Non-Uniform Schemes
The Mathematical Limit of Ternary Systems: Why 1.58 Bits?

outline.chapter_title: Architecture Design: The BitNet b1.58 Model
outline.description: This chapter provides a deep dive into the architectural specifics of BitNet b1.58. It details how standard Transformer components are modified to support ternary weights and low-bit activations, ensuring compatibility with modern open-source ecosystems like LLaMA while maximizing efficiency.
subtopics: Replacing nn.Linear with BitLinear
Weight Quantization: The AbsMean Function and RoundClip Operator
Activation Quantization: Symmetric Scaling and Zero-Point Removal
Integrating LLaMA Components: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, and Rotary Embeddings
Handling Biases and Normalization in Low-Precision Contexts

outline.description: Here, we explore how BitNet b1.58 is trained from scratch. The chapter outlines the data recipes, token counts, and baseline configurations used to ensure a fair comparison against full-precision models. It emphasizes the importance of training conditions in achieving parity with FP16 models.
subtopics: Training From Scratch vs. Fine-Tuning Quantized Models
Data Recipes: RedPajama and StableLM Datasets
Baseline Configuration: Reproducing FP16 LLaMA Models
Evaluation Metrics: Perplexity, Zero-Shot Accuracy, and End-Task Performance
Hyperparameters and Token Counts (100B to 2T)

outline.description: This chapter analyzes the core result: that 1.58-bit models can match full-precision performance. It breaks down the empirical results across various model sizes (3B to 70B) and benchmarks, highlighting the threshold where bit-wise models become competitive.
subtopics: Perplexity Trends Across Model Sizes (WikiText2 and C4)
Zero-Shot Benchmark Results (ARC, HellaSwag, Winogrande, etc.)
The 3B Threshold: Where Parity is Achieved
Scaling Laws for 1-Bit Models: Closing the Gap with Size
Long-Horizon Training Results: The 2 Trillion Token Experiment
